project.name: spring-rest-sakila
project.purpose: A REST API service providing CRUD and complex query access to the MySQL Sakila sample database, exposing domain entities such as actors, films, customers, staff, locations, payments, rentals, and stores with role-based security and observability features.
functionality: CRUD operations for actors, films, customers, staff, locations (addresses and cities), payments, rentals, and stores
Complex queries with filtering and pagination for entities like films and actors
User authentication and JWT token issuance for stateless security
Role-based access control enforced via Spring Security annotations
Hypermedia-driven REST responses using Spring HATEOAS with links for navigation
Generation of API documentation using Spring REST Docs, OpenAPI, and Postman collections
Observability via Spring Boot Actuator and Micrometer with Prometheus metrics endpoint
Sales reporting by category and store
project.architecture_style: Layered RESTful service architecture with domain-driven design influences and hypermedia-driven REST API

architecture.summary: The project is structured as a layered Spring Boot application exposing RESTful endpoints for domain entities of the Sakila database. It uses controllers to handle HTTP requests, services to encapsulate business logic, repositories for data access, and assemblers to convert domain DTOs into HATEOAS-compliant response models. Security is enforced via Spring Security with JWT authentication and role-based access control. The build and deployment are managed with Gradle Kotlin DSL, supporting modern Java 17 features. Observability and API documentation are integrated into the build and runtime.
patterns: Role-based access control with Spring Security @Secured annotations
Builder pattern for filtering options in query methods
Use of DTOs and assemblers for response model construction
Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State (HATEOAS) for REST responses
Exception handling delegated to service layer or global handlers
data_flow: Client sends HTTP requests to REST controllers
Controllers validate and parse requests, then delegate to service layer
Service layer executes business logic, interacts with repositories for data persistence
Repositories perform database operations on MySQL Sakila schema
Service layer returns domain DTOs to controllers
Controllers use assemblers to build HATEOAS response models
Controllers return HTTP responses with appropriate status codes and headers
Security layer authenticates requests using JWT tokens and enforces role-based access
Observability data collected via Spring Boot Actuator and Micrometer exposed to Prometheus
